author: Mark Atwood
text: API contract confidence (supplement pass): 30% chance of missed issue. Most confident: JMAP-ic0j.53 (principal.rs:121 bypass — verified by reading handlers.rs:78-80 directly), JMAP-ic0j.54-55 (Option<String> for typed-spec values — typed alternatives are already used elsewhere in the same trait), JMAP-ic0j.57 (re-export gap — visible by inspection of lib.rs:49-69 vs backend.rs pub items), JMAP-ic0j.58 (compute_utc_times Result-less tuple — direct type-signature read), JMAP-ic0j.60 (SetDefaultResult missing new() — direct comparison to ParseResult::new in same file). Least confident: JMAP-ic0j.56 (ParseResult name collision — workspace-policy call about whether bare in-module naming is acceptable for extension-local types; could be opinion), JMAP-ic0j.59 (From<E> missing — engineering basis is consistency with #[from] elsewhere in workspace but reasonable people disagree about ?-operator ergonomics), JMAP-ic0j.63 (realistic-demo-ids stability statement — depends on whether the feature is intended to be public-facing; the maintainer's intent is undocumented in either direction), JMAP-ic0j.67 (CannotCalculateOccurrences no detail — marked opinion). Uncertainty driven by: did not run cargo public-api to enumerate the actual exposed surface; did not check whether kith or stoa consumers depend on the calendars module path directly; did not cross-reference all 7 server-sibling extension crates for the realistic-demo-ids divergence; did not run cargo doc to inspect rendered rustdoc HTML for the doc-section gaps. Would raise confidence if: (a) ran cargo public-api against feature-on and feature-off builds; (b) grepped for downstream consumer imports of jmap_calendars_server::backend::*; (c) checked the canonical mail-server's git history for prior deliberation on the ParseResult-vs-MdnParseResult naming choice.
